verdictRule: ACCEPT only if no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX. I found neither.
verdictBasis: Every dispatched attack was run and every one was refuted against live bytes. The single MUST-FIX carried forward from the frozen predecessor, CLAUDE-G21FXV18-M-1, is landed exactly as its requiredFix specified and no further. A leaf-by-leaf diff against frozen g21-fixture-corpus.v18 shows 443 leaves against 428, zero leaves removed, fifteen added (the predecessorV18 block, doesNot[41], findingDisposition.claudeV18M1, three recordedInputs entries) and twenty-five changed, of which twenty-two are pure speaker-rename v18 -> v19 and exactly three are semantic: $.version 18 -> 19, $.purpose restated to this version's job, and $.basedOn.predecessorV15.role restored to the recorded landing target. Nothing else moved.

attacksRun.measurement: The finding's requiredFix was: restore $.basedOn.predecessorV15.role to 'Findings land at g21-fixture-corpus.v16.' The subject's leaf now reads verbatim 'Predecessor. Unmoved. Unrecorded. Frozen g21-fixture-corpus.v15 Stage A Claude REJECT 1 MUST-FIX CLAUDE-G21FXV15-M-1, 1 SHOULD-FIX CLAUDE-G21FXV15-S-1; Codex REJECT 1 unlabeled MUST-FIX. Findings land at g21-fixture-corpus.v16. Do not record g21-fixture-corpus.v15 as current. Not this artifact's version number.' This agrees with the ADOPTED D-335 register sentence at COORD line 19999 ('Findings land at g21-fixture-corpus.v16.'). The finding also said 'No byte, digest, platform token, count, or any other leaf is affected' - the leaf diff confirms that: this is the only basedOn role whose change is not a pure speaker-rename, and no digest, platform token or count moved. $.findingDisposition.claudeV18M1 records the landing and its text matches the byte actually written.

attacksRun.attack: predecessorV15.role Findings land rewritten off g21-fixture-corpus.v16
attacksRun.measurement: The leaf names g21-fixture-corpus.v16 and nothing else. I confirmed the speaker-rename pass did not re-sweep it: normalizing the frozen v18 leaf by substituting v18 -> v19 does NOT reproduce the v19 leaf, which is precisely how a re-swept leaf would have presented. The v18 -> v19 rename touched 22 other leaves and left this one at v16, the inverse of the defect that produced CLAUDE-G21FXV18-M-1.

Both remain landed and I verified each disposition against the bytes it claims rather than accepting the attestation. claudeV17M1 claims basedOn.leftoverJoinV13.role names g21 leftover-join.v17 (D-336) as current; that role reads 'Current recorded G21 leftover remasurement is g21 leftover-join.v17 (D-336) until a recordable successor is adopted.' claudeV17S1 claims doesNot charges remasurement and failsIf charges it; doesNot[39] is 'Does not remasure g21 leftover-join.v17.' and failsIf[19] is 'g21 leftover-join.v17 is remasured'. Neither leaf appears in the changed set against frozen v18, so neither regressed. $.basedOn.predecessorV17.role is byte-identical to the frozen predecessor's and correctly still reads 'Findings land at g21-fixture-corpus.v18.'

The only staleness the subject asserts is at $.basedOn.d336.role and $.basedOn.leftoverJoinV17.role and is scoped to 'the D-335 prefix-one-over-posthandshake injection', which is verbatim the D-336 recorded measurement at COORD lines 20165-20167. advisories.note: The restated purpose drops two clauses the predecessor carried, 'Do not invent a D-002 platform list.' and 'Do not copy onto Windows.', along with the v17-specific clauses that no longer apply. No standing is lost: both prohibitions remain live at doesNot[13] and doesNot[14], in $.whatIsNotAuthored ('a D-002 platform list', 'Windows as a copied platform'), and failsIf[5] charges failure if a D-002 platform list is invented. I verified on disk that no Windows copy exists. Recording this only so a later reader does not read the shorter purpose as a narrowed charge.

The fixture directory lineage runs independently of the corpus version lineage: corpus v13/v14 authored into fixtures/g21.v12/, corpus v16 into fixtures/g21.v15/, and corpus v17/v18/v19 into fixtures/g21.v16/. The offset is conventional and the bytes are stable and unmoved across the three corpus versions, and the subject documents the path shape ('fixtures/g21.v16/<platform-with-slash-replaced-by-dash>/'). It does not, however, carry the disclaimer it applies to the leftover-join lineage ('different lineages; their version numbers are unrelated') for the fixture directory. A future successor could add the same one-line disclaimer for fixture directories. Not a defect in this file: no claim here is false.
